analysis.title: Weekly Market Guide
key_insights: Raymond James keeps an upward bias on equities into year-end, citing a seasonally strong period and improving fundamentals.

About 74% of S&P 500 constituents are down more than 10% from their 52-week highs, while the cap-weighted index is 0.5% below its all-time high. Mega-cap strength is masking weakness in the average stock.

Base case is sideways consolidation and rotation, not a broader pullback. A stabilization in interest rates could pull capital back into recently pressured areas, funded by profit-taking in mega-cap growth and high-beta stocks.

Q3 2026 earnings expectations are elevated. Consensus is for about 28% y/y EPS growth, driven mainly by Energy and Technology. Last quarter's upside surprise was about 26%, which will be hard to repeat.
Small-caps and the equal-weight S&P 500 holding their 200-day moving averages is the breadth signal to watch. A break below both would raise the risk of a larger S&P 500 pullback.
Oil prices and interest rates are the key drivers of the next directional move. Further rises in yields and crude could pressure stocks, while relief from high rates could allow an upside breakout.
September core CPI came in hotter than expected on 10/14, and Treasury yields backed up that day.

10-year yield momentum is waning: RSI is coming off overbought levels and MACD has made a bearish crossover. The 20-day moving average is the next inflection point. A break below it could signal yields no longer have a path of least resistance higher.
Historically, the S&P 500 struggles in the first 9 months of midterm election years (not the case in 2026), but October through year-end is notably stronger.
Raymond James would not rule out additional bouts of volatility, and views consolidation and weakness as opportunities to selectively add exposure.

Last quarter's earnings exceeded expectations by about 26% (reported, Q2 2026). Raymond James expects positive surprises again but a smaller magnitude.
